title: Guard, Reserve and duty-status authorities (Operation Sentinel, Module 01)
governing_rule: Eligibility follows the legal authority printed on the orders, not the character of the mission. Never infer status from the mission (this is why service_record.legal_authority is required for Guard/Reserve in migration 0009). These authorities classify duty; they do not produce a benefit determination. Sentinel's determination logic is carried as rule leads (below) and stays withheld behind G1.

authorities.label: AGR — organize, administer, recruit, instruct, train
Other full-time National Guard duty — no emergency declaration

tier_caveat_text: Time under 12301(h), 12304a or 12304b counts toward Chapter 33 eligibility but cannot raise the benefit tier for terms beginning before 1 Aug 2018.

rule_leads.lead: 90 cumulative qualifying days since 11 Sep 2001 meets the eligibility threshold; percentage tier scales with total time. Drill, annual training and State Active Duty do not count.
rule_leads.caveat: At 85–89 days, orders can sometimes be extended before they expire, almost never after (March 2020 Guard activations were extended for this reason).

rule_leads.lead: Requires SELRES status and a six-year obligation entered on or after 1 Jul 1985 plus a secondary-school credential. Not vested: ends on transfer out of SELRES (IRR/ING), with tuition-recoupment exposure mid-course.
$4,500 per fiscal year, $250 per semester hour, 18 semester hours; master's $350 per credit hour up to 39 (Army figures). Coast Guard SELRES: $4,500 / $250, one master's only.
rule_leads.caveat: FTA pays first; schools deduct it before billing VA. Coast Guard figures rest on a secondary source (confirm COMDTINST). Re-verify FY27 rates after 1 Oct.

rule_leads.lead: Funds credentials that need not align to the MOS but must retain a military nexus. Since 19 Mar 2026 every TA and CA request needs supervisor or commander approval in ArmyIgnitED.
rule_leads.caveat: Officer restriction inferred from an agency summary, not the ALARACT itself.

rule_leads.citation: INA 329; 8 USC 1440; USCIS Policy Manual vol. 12 pt. I ch. 3
rule_leads.lead: Selected Reserve membership during a designated period of hostilities (11 Sep 2001 to present, open) is qualifying service; no activation, deployment or minimum period required. IRR/ING do not qualify on this path.
rule_leads.correction_on_record: An earlier draft said drilling status generally does not qualify. That was wrong and is logged rather than silently fixed because it understated a member's rights.

rule_leads.citation: Samma v. DoD; service implementing messages
rule_leads.lead: SUPERSEDED. The requirement no longer exists; certification needs only an honest assessment that service has been honorable, and the first O-6 in the chain must process it within 30 days.
Entitlements from separate service periods may be used in any order up to the 48-month aggregate cap with no forced election (held for Ch. 30 and Ch. 33).
rule_leads.caveat: Extension to a Ch. 1606 + Ch. 33 pairing is reasoning by analogy, not holding; Perkins (No. 24-6515, Vet. App.) may bear on it.

rule_leads.lead: Most state benefits key off a state-law definition of veteran requiring federal active duty. Guard service of only drill, annual training and State Active Duty often fails it (Texas Hazlewood needs 181 days).

Civilian employment does not create veteran status or veterans' preference. A civilian who is also Guard/Reserve is assessed under the military status. Coast Guard permanent civilians are documented as TA-eligible; do not extend by analogy.

Sunset; legacy users may appear in records

review_cadence: Statute tracks the NDAA (annually around December). DoD instructions and Army regulations track their own review dates. ALARACTs, NAVADMINs and COMDTINSTs need a monthly sweep. State tuition and tax records expire at each legislative session close (most between March and June). Federal rates reset with the fiscal year on 1 October.

coverage.note: A stub is not an absence of benefits.
